english.title: Off duty seaman - ability to carry out duties in an emergency impaired by drink / drugs - transport safety
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a professional seaman on a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SHIP..), at a time when you were not on duty, your ability to take action to protect the safety of passengers in the event of an emergency, as required by the nature or terms of your engagement or employment, was impaired because of

(A)_[drugs]_
(B)_[drink]_
(C)_[drink and drugs]_
(D)_[drink or drugs]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 79(2) and 82 of the Railways and Transport Safety Act 2003.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

in the event of an emergency

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This offence relates to an off duty professional seaman ONLY, the Act does not provide a comparable offence in relation to a master or pilot which seems to intimate that they have a constant responsibility.

other.powersofarrest: Section 85(1) provides that a constable may arrest a person without a warrant if the constable reasonably suspects that the person has committed this offence and is still under the influence of drink or drugs.
other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
